launch_note: Pinned at launch (this is what the pre-launch log entry, dddf30c, records). This is a shared checkout: three PRs (fe4b32f, a940376, a99b573) self-merged to main during this run's ~8h10m wall clock, plus two docs-only commits (ae29d38, f920fb8). Each of the 36 subprocess invocations (18 decompose + 18 eval) is spawned fresh by the orchestrator and reads the CURRENT file on disk at invocation time, so different cells of this one sweep ran under different HEAD commits - see commit_provenance_per_cell below and the verification that none of the intervening commits are behaviorally relevant to this run's decompose or eval-metric-value code paths.

verification_that_intervening_commits_do.method: git diff between the launch pin (6831ee5) and the final HEAD observed (a99b573) restricted to every file this sweep's decompose+eval path reads.
verification_that_intervening_commits_do.configs/pool_sweep.json, configs/similar: byte-identical across the whole range (git diff empty) - not touched by any of the 5 intervening commits.
verification_that_intervening_commits_do.configs/decomposer.json: gained one no-op block in fe4b32f (PR #43): 'hop_source': 'gold' + a 'hop_predictions' interface stub. 'gold' is exactly the pre-existing implicit behaviour (a guided run's hop count comes from the query's own depth); this sweep's cells are all the unguided/no-conditions-block arm (guided:false, no 'conditions' key in decomposer.json), so hop_source is resolved and recorded as metadata but never reaches a prompt. Confirmed structurally in components/decomposer/run_decomposer.py's resolve_hop_source(): guided=false is disjoint from every branch that changes behaviour (all of them require guided=true).
verification_that_intervening_commits_do.components/decomposer/run_decomposer.py: the only diff across the whole range (fe4b32f/a940376, 292 lines) is resolve_hop_source/join_predicted_hops and the --hop-predictions CLI flag - all new code paths gated on guided=true or an explicit 'hop_source' condition key, neither of which this sweep's config sets. No change to prompt rendering, generation call, decoding, or the pinned-eval-set / hops loading logic this sweep's retrieval-input branch actually uses.
verification_that_intervening_commits_do.scripts/musique_decompositions_evaluator: a99b573 (PR #44) adds four new per-item/aggregate columns (chain_validity, break_exact_match, sari, ged) plus one new config block ('break_metrics'). composite_score_weights and composite_step_count_error_scale are byte-identical in the config diff; the script's own docstring and _statistics_available() treat the four new metrics as strictly additive (never enter composite_score, no existing metric changes value). PER_ITEM_SCHEMA is unchanged ('musique_decomposition_per_item/1'), so old- and new-code per-item files remain mutually comparable.
verification_that_intervening_commits_do.conclusion: predictions (results.json) are behaviourally identical regardless of which of the 4 decompose-stage commits produced them; eval_metrics.json / eval_per_item.json for all 18 cells carry 4 extra additive columns beyond what a strict 6831ee5-pinned eval would have written, and every metric this row headlines (step_f1, ordered_step_accuracy, hop_count_exact_match_rate, composite_score, rouge_l_f1, exact_match_rate) is computed by unchanged code under unchanged weights. Per the coordinator's instruction, this run's numbers are NOT a re-score under the new metrics (the new columns are recorded per schema in eval_metrics.json but not used anywhere in this row's comparison) - the nine-arm re-score under the new metrics is a separate, later assignment.

preflight_check_typed_uniform_distinctne.question: The dev sample carries no question_masked_typed/question_masked_uniform fields (exp-006's own flag). Does that make the typed/uniform retrieval modes a silent fallback to raw, i.e. are 12 of 18 cells duplicate compute?
preflight_check_typed_uniform_distinctne.evidence: check_question_similarity.py's own docstring: it NER-masks queries on the fly when the query file lacks the masked fields. Verified directly on exp-006's committed runs/pool_sweep/similarity/size2000_<balance>_trial0/top20.jsonl (all 3 balances): typed_top_k and uniform_top_k candidate-id lists differ from raw_top_k on 750/750 rows in every balance (0 rows identical across all three modes).
preflight_check_typed_uniform_distinctne.conclusion: typed and uniform are genuinely distinct retrieval conditions here; no cells were cut. Issue #14's own comment independently records the same finding.
